target_band.cite: Fact sheet valuation table (research/FSLR/factsheet-2026-10-07.md): bull basis reverts P/E to its 5y min 14.6x (179.80x14.6/11.1=236.49) vs. EV/EBITDA to its 5y min 10.1x (179.80x10.1/7.5=242.13), both at flat earnings; half the spread between the two implied prices divided by the target = ~1.2%.

base.probability_evidence: The note flags that margins are at five-year highs and the fact sheet cannot split 45X credits from core operating profit (note section 2), and a securities class action plus patent litigation are unresolved (note section 6) — these argue for stasis rather than a directional break until Q3 earnings (Oct 29) confirm or refute margin durability, which is why 'hold' carries the largest single weight (45%).

target_band.cite: Fact sheet valuation table (research/FSLR/factsheet-2026-10-07.md): base basis holds both P/E (11.1x) and EV/EBITDA (7.5x) at current levels with earnings flat, so both anchors imply the unchanged current price (179.80); the anchors agree, so band = 0.

bear.probability_evidence: TTM gross/operating margins sit at or near five-year highs while leaning on 45X credits and tariff protection (note section 2); FY2022's -10.7% operating margin shows how fast this business can swing (factsheet Quality table); short interest rose 11.6% MoM to 10.35% of float (ST) and a securities class action is live (note section 6); probability is raised by 0.05 above a symmetric default for the macro overlay's moderate bear tilt on rising real yields and widening HY spreads (research/FSLR/2026-10-07-macro.md).

target_band.cite: Fact sheet valuation table (research/FSLR/factsheet-2026-10-07.md): bear basis applies the same operating-margin reversion (33.6%->26.7%, income statement) to earnings while holding the multiple fixed at its current level for both P/E (11.1x) and EV/EBITDA (7.5x); since neither multiple moves, both anchors scale by the identical earnings ratio and imply the same price, so band = 0.
